comments.body:
I reviewed the full solution against the problem statement and verified its mathematical claims.

**Assessment.** The existing proof is essentially complete and correct. It (R1) locates the defective step as the conditional-symmetry assumption Pr(mine larger | observed value)=1/2 for *every* observed value; (R2) shows the unique belief structure forcing that symmetry is improper (multiplicatively 2-periodic densities; canonically the log-uniform dt/t) with divergent expectations, so E[Y-X]=infinity-infinity is undefined; and (R3) states and proves the unified normative principle: base the decision on E_pi[Delta U] under a prior making that expectation well defined (integrable), using genuine posteriors pi(.|data) rather than symmetry-imposed probabilities. Under an exchangeable proper prior the swap map gives E_pi[Delta U]=0, so no symmetric exchange is advantageous to both parties and "always switch" is never optimal for all observations. The necktie case reduces to the zero-sum identity E[G_A]+E[G_B]=0 (Fubini, integrability) plus exchangeability => both expectations 0.

**Numerical checks performed.**
- Exponential prior f(t)=e^{-t}: sign of E[Y|X=x]-x equals sign of 2f(x)-f(x/2), changing at x=2 ln 2 ~ 1.386 (confirmed); simulated E[Y-X] ~ 0. Matches Lemma 1 / Remark 1.
- Log-uniform improper prior f(t)=1/t: dyadic partial sums of E[Y] grow geometrically (23.8, 192.0, 3072.0), confirming divergence.

**Fix applied.** The only soft spot was the derivation of E[Y]=+infinity in the improper-prior lemma, which appealed to a "ranges over the same values" symmetry remark. I replaced it with a direct computation:
E[Y] = integral (1/2 * 2x f(x) + 1/2 * (x/2) f(x/2)) dx = integral (x f(x) + (x/4) f(x/2)) dx >= integral x f(x) dx = +infinity,
the last integral being +infinity by the dyadic-block computation already established for E[X]. This makes the divergence rigorous without invoking symmetry.

All theorem/lemma/proof/enumerate environments are balanced (checked programmatically); no LaTeX toolchain is installed so compilation was skipped. I consider the proof complete and am marking the issue resolved.
